Add ability to memory-map contents of BPF array map. This is extremely useful
for working with BPF global data from userspace programs. It allows to avoid
typical bpf_map_{lookup
and usability.
There had to be special considerations for map freezing
writable memory view into a frozen map. To solve this issue
mmap-ing is happening under mutex now:
- if map is already frozen
- if map has writable memory mappings active (accounted in map->writecnt)
map freezing will keep failing with -EBUSY;
- once number of writable memory mappings drops to zero
performed again.
Only non-per-CPU plain arrays are supported right now. Maps with spinlocks
can't be memory mapped either.
For BPF_F_MMAPABLE array
column2: memory allocation has to be done through vmalloc()

column1: to be mmap()'able. We also need to make sure that array data memory is
page-sized and page-aligned
column2: so we over-allocate memory in such a way that

column1: struct bpf_array is at the end of a single page of memory with array->value
being aligned with the start of the second page. On deallocation we need to
accomodate this memory arrangement to free vmalloc()'ed memory correctly.
One important consideration regarding how memory-mapping subsystem functions.
Memory-mapping subsystem provides few optional callbacks
and close().  close() is called for each memory region that is unmapped
that users can decrease their reference counters and free up resources
necessary. open() is *almost* symmetrical: it's called for each memory region
that is being mapped
column2: **except** the very first one. So bpf_map_mmap does

column1: initial refcnt bump
column2: while open() will do any extra ones after that. Thus

column1: number of close() calls is equal to number of open() calls plus one more.
